$comment: Bridge configuration. This file is tracked; machine-specific values belong
in config/bridge.local.json (gitignored), which is shallow-merged over this.
'peer' is deliberately null here. A RustDesk ID is the address of a specific
machine -- publishing one invites connection attempts against it -- so real
IDs live only in bridge.local.json. Set it there, or pass --peer.
No credential appears in this repo. RustDesk stores the peer password in its
own encrypted config; the bridge only ever names a peer.

$write_note: Writing global options runs RustDesk elevated and triggers UAC.
Turn this on deliberately, and keep allow_write narrow.

$note: Each entry is [local_port, remote_host, remote_port] -- the schema RustDesk
persists in peers/<id>.toml. RustDesk binds the listener to 0.0.0.0, NOT to
127.0.0.1, so an open forward exposes the remote service to your whole local
network for as long as the session lasts. That is why this is opt-in and why
each forward has to be named rather than allowed by pattern.
The pixel layer sends real mouse and keyboard events to the remote machine.
It is off by default and there is no way to undo a click.
